AWPTCM-T33233.objective:
• A port with no pluggable present defaults to automatic speed and duplex negotiation.
  • Inserting a supported pluggable results in successful autonegotiation and link establishment.
  • A port configured for Auto speed and duplex establishes a link with a compliant link partner.
  • Link establishment succeeds when one side is set to Auto and the partner is forced to a supported speed or duplex.
  • The port accurately reports Auto mode together with the negotiated speed and duplex values.
  • Link status is correctly reported as up once autonegotiation completes.
  • Automatic speed and duplex negotiation produces a working link across all supported configurations with a compliant partner.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.
Verify default behavior and autonegotiation with no pluggable present (Auto as default for speed and duplex). Insert a supported pluggable and confirm autonegotiation occurs and link is established.
Set the port to Auto for speed and duplex. With link partner also on Auto, confirm link is established and port reports as Auto while showing the negotiated speed/duplex.
Vary link partner configurations across supported speeds and duplex modes (one side Auto, both sides Auto, partner forced to supported rates). Confirm successful link establishment in each case.
Test with incompatible partner speed/duplex settings. Confirm link does not establish (or is correctly reported as down).

Hot-insert and hot-remove supported pluggables while the port is set to Auto. Confirm link negotiation occurs cleanly on insertion and link status updates correctly on removal. Speak to the SVT team to get an arrangement of pluggables for testing.
Where the platform and media support it, test with EcoMode enabled and disabled on Auto-negotiated links. Confirm EcoMode behavior and that link remains stable.

## Gaps Noted
No specific automated tests were confirmed as related coverage for this case, so while Zephyr flags it as covered by an auto-test, that claim is not currently substantiated by any identified automation artefact. Auto/Auto link negotiation is the kind of behaviour that automated checks can reasonably confirm at the level of a link reaching an established state with the expected negotiated speed and duplex. Even assuming such coverage exists, the less well-covered areas are typically the negotiation transients and edge conditions — renegotiation after link flaps, mismatched or forced peer settings, and behaviour across cable or media changes — along with the observability that a manual tester relies on, such as advertised-capability exchange, negotiation status reporting, and log or counter evidence that the outcome was genuinely auto-negotiated rather than defaulted. Until a concrete automated test is identified, this should be treated as an unverified coverage gap rather than confirmed automation.

sequence.action: On the DUT with no pluggable installed in the target port, read the port default configuration with 'show interface portX.Y.Z' (or 'show interface portX.Y.Z status').
sequence.verify: Output reports the port's configured speed as 'auto'/'Auto-negotiate' and duplex as 'auto', confirming Auto is the factory default for both speed and duplex on an empty port.

sequence.action: After a supported pluggable is present in the target port (insertion is physical — see notes), read the port state with 'show interface portX.Y.Z' and 'show system pluggable'.
sequence.verify: Pluggable is detected/recognized, the port link state reads 'up', and speed/duplex show negotiated values consistent with the pluggable's supported rate — proving autonegotiation completed and a link was established.

sequence.action: Enter configuration mode on the DUT port and explicitly set 'speed auto' and 'duplex auto'; ensure the link partner port is also configured for auto speed and auto duplex.
sequence.verify: 'show running-config interface portX.Y.Z' reflects speed auto and duplex auto on both ends with no config errors.

sequence.action: With both DUT and partner on Auto/Auto, bring the link up and read 'show interface portX.Y.Z status' on the DUT.
sequence.verify: Link state = up; the port reports negotiation mode as Auto AND displays the concrete negotiated speed and duplex (e.g., 1000/full), confirming Auto mode is reported together with the negotiated values.

sequence.action: For each supported speed S, force the link partner port to fixed 'speed S' / 'duplex full' while leaving the DUT on Auto/Auto; re-check link after each change with 'show interface portX.Y.Z status'.
sequence.verify: For every supported S, DUT link state = up and DUT-reported negotiated speed equals S with matching duplex, confirming Auto-vs-forced-supported combinations establish a link at the partner's forced rate.

sequence.action: For each supported speed, set both DUT and partner to the same fixed supported speed/duplex, then repeat with both back on Auto/Auto; read 'show interface portX.Y.Z status' after each configuration.
sequence.verify: Link state = up in every supported configuration; when both are Auto the negotiated speed equals the highest common supported rate, confirming a working link across all supported configurations.

sequence.action: Optionally, send bidirectional test traffic across the negotiated link (Scapy transmit, tcpdump capture on partner) for a representative negotiated configuration.
sequence.verify: All transmitted frames are received with no loss and no CRC/error-counter increments in 'show interface portX.Y.Z' counters, proving the auto-negotiated link is genuinely functional (not merely reported up).

sequence.action: Configure an incompatible pairing: leave DUT on Auto and force the partner to a duplex the DUT cannot match / an unsupported rate (e.g., partner fixed 'duplex half' or a speed the pluggable does not support), then read 'show interface portX.Y.Z status'.
sequence.verify: DUT link state is reported as 'down' (or the link fails to establish / shows a duplex-mismatch condition); no valid negotiated speed+duplex is presented, confirming incompatible settings do not bring the link up.

sequence.action: With the port set to Auto/Auto, perform a hot-remove of the supported pluggable (physical — see notes) and read 'show interface portX.Y.Z' and 'show system pluggable' plus the event log.
sequence.verify: On removal, link state transitions to 'down', pluggable no longer listed, and a link-down/pluggable-removed log entry is generated — confirming link status updates correctly on removal.

sequence.action: Hot-insert the supported pluggable back into the Auto/Auto port (physical — see notes) and read 'show interface portX.Y.Z status' and the event log.
sequence.verify: Autonegotiation re-runs cleanly, link state returns to 'up' with expected negotiated speed/duplex, and a link-up/pluggable-inserted log entry is generated.

sequence.action: Where platform/media support it, enable EcoMode (e.g., 'ecofriendly lpi') on the DUT port over an established Auto-negotiated link, then read 'show interface portX.Y.Z status' and 'show ecofriendly' over a short soak.
sequence.verify: EcoMode/LPI reports as enabled, link remains 'up' and stable (no flaps / no error-counter increments), and negotiated speed/duplex are unchanged.

sequence.action: Disable EcoMode ('no ecofriendly lpi') on the same Auto-negotiated port and re-read 'show interface portX.Y.Z status' and 'show ecofriendly'.
sequence.verify: EcoMode/LPI reports as disabled, link remains 'up' and stable with the same negotiated speed/duplex, confirming EcoMode toggling does not disrupt the auto-negotiated link.

step4.rationale: The three selected legacy scripts are MDI/MDIX polarity suites whose TestSet topology assumes a pluggable is already seated for the whole run and whose TestCases only assert configured speed/duplex/polarity plus link-up via checkLinkStatus/checkConfiguredPort helpers. None of them exercise the empty-port default read, explicit config-mode auto/auto entry, forced-partner-vs-auto-DUT sweeps, traffic validation, incompatible-duplex link-down proof, hot-remove/insert, or EcoMode toggling required by this sequence, so a new script composed from these helper patterns is needed rather than extending one chassis.

per_step.gap: TestCase_1 in each script checks speed/duplex=auto only after the pluggable is already installed; none reads port defaults on an empty port before pluggable insertion.

configure() logs 'show sys'/'show sys plug' and TestCase_1 confirms link-up with auto/auto, but no assertion explicitly ties pluggable detection to negotiated rate consistent with the pluggable's supported speed.
No script shows an explicit config-mode 'speed auto'/'duplex auto' entry followed by a running-config check on both DUT and partner; existing cases only assert resulting state.
Confirms auto/auto configured and link up, but does not assert the status output shows the concrete negotiated speed/duplex value alongside the Auto mode label.

No case forces only the link-partner to a fixed speed while leaving the DUT on Auto/Auto; the speed-variant cases (e.g. TestCase_6-10) appear to change both ends together, not asymmetric Auto-vs-forced pairs, and don't sweep every supported speed.

Existing speed variants toggle among auto-1000/100/10 combos for polarity testing but don't set fully fixed (non-auto) matching speeds on both ends across the whole supported range, nor explicitly verify highest-common-rate negotiation when reverting to auto/auto.
No Scapy/tcpdump frame-loss or CRC-counter validation exists; scripts only check port/link status, not traffic-level correctness.
No case configures an incompatible duplex/speed pairing to confirm the DUT link fails or reports down; all existing cases target working link configurations.
No hot-remove of the pluggable is performed; TestSet topology assumes the pluggable remains inserted for the whole script run, with no event-log check for removal.
No hot-insert-after-removal step or link-up/pluggable-inserted event-log verification exists.
No EcoMode/'ecofriendly lpi' enablement or 'show ecofriendly' check exists in any selected script.
No EcoMode disablement/regression check exists in any selected script.
